what_expired: Twice now. #1086 chose 900 against a 165s median and 393s p90 over 28 runs; by 2026-08-31 the p90 over 69 runs was 884s, more than double, and 900 was re-justified against that. On 2026-09-04 the job had got FASTER, not slower: median 174s to 63s and worst 2,182s to 961s, because #1096 moved the app build out of the per-entry cost. 900 then sat inside the dense middle and the guard said so. Read the caveat below before treating these numbers as the steady state.
why_850: Chosen from where the distribution actually is, not picked round (L172). Over 95 runs: median 63s, p75 349s, p90 756s, worst 961s. There is a real gap between 793s and 869s and 850 sits in it, so the deadline is not inside the dense middle where a small shift carries many runs across at once. Seven runs are at or over it, 7%, so it is a tail rather than ordinary operation. Setup is measured at 24s median and 31s at worst, so 850 leaves 950s of headroom under the job's 1,800s cap and the deadline is comfortably what fires.
caveat: These 95 runs are weighted toward changes that touch little Swift, because the work in the days before 2026-09-04 was mostly Python and CI tooling. A wide Swift diff is exactly the case this deadline is about and is under-represented here, so re-measure after a stretch of app work rather than assuming the tail has really shrunk (L354).
